name: Our Little World — Begin Small, Build Together
goal: Help a consented parent save a first meaningful, parent-approved memory and then experience the shared baby-book value.

pre_activation_track.entry: new account plus explicit marketing consent and no moment_saved
pre_activation_track.exit: first moment_saved, consent revoked, unsubscribe, complaint, hard bounce, deletion pending, or account deletion

post_activation_track.entry: first moment_saved plus valid marketing consent
post_activation_track.exit: consent revoked, unsubscribe, complaint, hard bounce, deletion pending, account deletion, or sequence completion

architecture.numbering_decision: Do not use 1 of 6. The first saved memory moves a parent between tracks, so rigid numbering would become inaccurate.

entry.trigger: olw-parent-welcome-v2 may be applied once only after server-authored marketing consent and role=parent_or_guardian

frequency_policy.timezone: recipient timezone when reliable; otherwise account default

tracking.open_tracking_role: diagnostic only; never primary optimization signal

provider.name: Mailchimp
provider.migration: Replace the inactive five-email draft with two behavior-triggered tracks. Retain the old flow as rollback evidence until both tracks pass tests.

emails.internal_name: Founder welcome — why the camera roll was not enough
emails.audience: Consented parent or guardian before first moment_saved
emails.primary_job: Give the parent permission to begin with one meaningful moment, not a baby-book project.
emails.reader_tension: The camera roll is full, but turning it into a family story feels like an overdue project.
emails.useful_micro_action: Choose one recent photo and add one line about why it matters.
emails.product_behavior: Save a parent-approved photo or note as a private family memory.
emails.subject: Why our camera roll wasn't enough
subject_alternatives: Why our camera roll wasn't enough
You do not need to catch up on the baby book
Start with the photo you still remember clearly
emails.preview: My wife and I wanted the story around our baby's photos—not another project for someday.
preview_alternatives: My wife and I wanted the story around our baby's photos—not another project for someday.
One photo and one honest line are enough to begin.
paragraphs: My wife and I kept taking photos and videos of our baby, just like everyone does. But when we tried to revisit them, the camera roll gave us files—not the family story we wanted to remember.
Our Little World began with that gap. It is a private place for the photos, firsts, voice notes, and letters we choose to keep, with the meaning still attached.
You do not need to organize the camera roll or reconstruct every month. Choose one recent photo that still feels close and add one line about why you kept it. That is a real beginning.

module.title: One photo + one line
module.detail: Not the best photo. Not the whole month. Just the moment whose story you still know.

emails.secondary_reply_interaction: Invite replies only after support@ourlittleworld.me monitoring is verified.
emails.exit_or_skip: Skip if moment_saved exists before send time.
emails.guardrail_metric: unsubscribe or complaint after the first send

emails.internal_name: First-memory micro-action — one photo, one line
emails.audience: Consented parent still before first moment_saved
emails.primary_job: Remove the pressure to choose a perfect or milestone-worthy first memory.
emails.reader_tension: Starting feels difficult because the first entry seems as though it should be important or complete.
emails.useful_micro_action: Choose an ordinary recent photo and write the detail the image cannot explain.
emails.product_behavior: The Add flow saves media with a written note to the private family timeline.
emails.subject: Try the photo that needs one sentence
subject_alternatives: Try the photo that needs one sentence
Your first memory does not need to be a milestone
The picture has the scene. Add the part it missed.
emails.preview: Choose an ordinary photo and write the detail only you would know.
preview_alternatives: Choose an ordinary photo and write the detail only you would know.
A useful first entry can be smaller than a milestone.
paragraphs: The best first memory is not necessarily the biggest milestone. It may be the photo that needs one sentence before its meaning disappears.
Choose something ordinary from the last few days: a look, a routine, the way a room felt. Then add the detail the image cannot hold by itself.
That small piece of context is what turns a file into part of the family story.

module.title: what happened
module.detail: Your one sentence can keep how it felt, what they were doing every day, or why you laughed.

emails.exit_or_skip: Skip and enter the post-activation track when moment_saved exists.

emails.audience: Consented parent still before first moment_saved, with permission-state-specific CTA where reliable
emails.primary_job: Explain the boundary between optional local discovery, a suggestion, and an approved saved memory.
emails.reader_tension: A parent may hesitate because family media and photo-library permissions feel sensitive.
emails.useful_micro_action: Review the permission choice and manually select one item if broad access is not wanted.
emails.product_behavior: Manual picking and optional local photo discovery; only selected or approved moments enter the private archive.
emails.subject: What Our Little World does with your photos
subject_alternatives: What Our Little World does with your photos
A suggestion is not a saved memory
You choose the photo access—and what gets kept
emails.preview: Discovery is optional. A memory enters the family space only through the product's documented save behavior.
preview_alternatives: Discovery is optional. A memory enters the family space only through the product's documented save behavior.
You control device permission, review, and what belongs in the private archive.
paragraphs: Family media deserves a clear boundary.

You choose what photo access to grant. Manual adds use the system picker or the permission on your device. Optional discovery can scan locally to surface likely moments for review. Selected manual imports and calibrated auto-saves are uploaded to the private family archive; nothing is posted to a public feed.
If broad library access does not feel right, keep it limited and add a photo manually. You should be able to begin without surrendering the choice.

module.title: The choices stay with you
items: Choose limited, full, or no photo-library access in device settings
Review or manually select what belongs
Change the permission later if you want

emails.exit_or_skip: Skip pre-activation track if moment_saved exists; branch CTA to device settings only when coarse permission state is reliable.
emails.success_event: moment_saved; photo_permission_granted is a supporting event, not activation
emails.guardrail_metric: permission-help clicks without moment_saved or elevated unsubscribe

emails.internal_name: Shared story — invite the other perspective
emails.audience: Activated consenting parent with one saved memory and no accepted second caregiver
emails.primary_job: Show why one other caregiver makes the archive more complete without creating a social feed.
emails.reader_tension: One person cannot see or remember every part of the early years.
emails.useful_micro_action: Invite the one caregiver who holds the other half of the ordinary story.
emails.product_behavior: The app can invite one other caregiver into the same private family space.
emails.subject: Invite the person who remembers the other half
subject_alternatives: Invite the person who remembers the other half
One family story, two points of view
The other caregiver noticed something you missed
emails.preview: Add one trusted caregiver to the private family space—without making another feed.
preview_alternatives: Add one trusted caregiver to the private family space—without making another feed.
The ordinary story gets richer when both people can add what they noticed.
paragraphs: One person never sees the whole beginning.
The other caregiver remembers a different joke, catches a different photo, and notices the routine you stopped seeing because you were inside it.
Invite that one person into the same private family space. The goal is not a bigger audience. It is one shared story with both points of view.

module.title: Two perspectives, one story
module.detail: Invite one trusted caregiver. Keep the circle small and the record shared.

emails.exit_or_skip: Skip if an accepted second caregiver already exists; do not send to a caregiver invitee as parent onboarding.
emails.success_event: caregiver_invite_created followed by invite_accepted; privacy-safe sync seams required
emails.guardrail_metric: invite CTA clicks without an accepted invitation

emails.audience: Activated consenting parent who has not created a First
emails.primary_job: Demonstrate that a First can preserve the context around change, not merely check a milestone box.
emails.reader_tension: Milestone lists can feel generic, pressured, or disconnected from the actual memory.
emails.useful_micro_action: Add one first and one detail that makes it specific to this family.
emails.product_behavior: The Firsts surface records milestones and their family-specific context.
emails.subject: A first is more than a milestone
subject_alternatives: A first is more than a milestone
Keep the detail beside the first
The milestone is the label. This is the story.
emails.preview: Record one change and the small detail that makes it yours.
preview_alternatives: Record one change and the small detail that makes it yours.
A first smile or step matters more when the family detail stays attached.
paragraphs: A milestone list can tell you what changed. It rarely keeps the part your family will actually repeat later.
In Firsts, record one change and add the detail around it: where you were, what happened just before, or the phrase everyone kept using afterward.
The milestone is the label. The detail is the family story.

module.title: Name the change. Keep the detail.
module.detail: One milestone, described in the language your family will recognize later.

emails.exit_or_skip: Skip if first_created exists before send time.

emails.internal_name: Gentle ritual — one sentence for later
emails.audience: Activated consenting parent who has not created a Letter
emails.primary_job: Introduce a sustainable, low-pressure writing ritual and invite useful founder feedback.
emails.reader_tension: Writing a letter for the future sounds meaningful but too important to begin casually.
emails.useful_micro_action: Write one sentence beginning with something noticed today.
emails.product_behavior: Letters supports private time-capsule writing for the child or partner.
emails.subject: Write one sentence for later
subject_alternatives: A letter does not have to begin like a letter
emails.preview: Begin with one thing you noticed today. Stop after one sentence if that is enough.
preview_alternatives: Begin with one thing you noticed today. Stop after one sentence if that is enough.
The quietest part of the baby book can start with a very small line.
paragraphs: A letter for later can feel too important to start. So do not start with a letter.
Start with one sentence: “Today I noticed…” Write the detail you would tell your future self if you could send a note forward in time. Stop there if that is enough.
The best ritual is the one that does not turn family life into homework. Our Little World should make the story easier to keep, then stay quiet.
If the product is helping—or asking too much—reply and tell me. I want to understand where it feels light and where it still feels like work.

module.title: Today I noticed…
module.detail: One true detail. No polished letter required.

emails.secondary_reply_interaction: Reply with where the product feels light or still feels like work; activate only after mailbox monitoring is verified.
emails.exit_or_skip: Skip if letter_created exists before send time.
emails.guardrail_metric: direct negative replies, unsubscribe, or CTA click without letter creation

activation_requirements: Authenticate ourlittleworld.me in Mailchimp and confirm SPF, DKIM, and DMARC alignment.
Verify support@ourlittleworld.me is monitored before sending reply invitations.
Implement explicit marketing-consent capture and server-authored audience eligibility; product account creation alone is insufficient.
Synchronize moment_saved exits and coarse role/permission state without sending private family content to Mailchimp.
Add privacy-safe caregiver invite, first_created, and letter_created outcome events before enabling those skips.
Keep gift purchase, gift delivery, redemption, billing, export, deletion, and security communications transactional and separate.
Render, link-check, accessibility-check, and inspect every HTML and plain-text version.
Send controlled tests to verified internal recipients and inspect receipt in representative clients.
Activate only after all gates pass; current audience contains zero recipients.
